title: On the road: traffic and driving
subtitle: give way, tailback, roadworthy
summary: Talk about traffic rules, offences and jams with precision - from breathalyser tests and penalty points to tailbacks, pile-ups and road rage.

lesson.heading: Junctions and crossings
lesson.text: In the UK you must **give way** - stop at a junction before entering a bigger road - at a **give-way sign** and at a roundabout, where traffic coming from the right has the **right of way**, that is, is allowed to go before other traffic. You must give way to pedestrians at a **pedestrian crossing**, often called a **zebra crossing** when it has black and white stripes.

examples.text: If it's a **give-way** sign you don't have to stop when the road is clear, but at a stop sign you always must.
Who has the **right of way** at a pedestrian crossing in your country - cars or pedestrians?
In some countries, **sounding** or **beeping** your horn is prohibited except in emergencies.
examples.note: beeping is less formal than sounding

lesson.heading: Driving offences
rows: not stopping at a red light
very dangerous driving, without any care for others
driving after consuming alcohol above the official limit
running into someone and not stopping
a test with an instrument you breathe into to measure your alcohol level
negative points added up over time, which can result in the loss of your licence
a fine given at the scene of the offence

lesson.heading: Is the car legal?
lesson.text: In the European Union, **exhaust emissions** - the waste gases produced by the vehicle - must meet certain standards, and the car must be **roadworthy**, that is, in a condition in which it can be driven safely. That includes a minimum depth of **tyre tread**; driving with a **bald** tyre, one that has lost its tread, is against the law.

examples.text: The permitted level of **emissions** is to be lowered in an attempt to reduce air pollution in big cities.
The man at the garage said my car wasn't **roadworthy**.
The police officer looked at two of my tyres and said they were **bald**.

lesson.heading: Traffic jams
lesson.text: A **tailback** is a line of slow or stopped traffic. **Congestion** is a situation in which there is a lot of traffic that cannot move - in some cities drivers pay a **congestion charge** to enter the centre. A **toll** is a charge you pay to use a road or bridge.

examples.text: It was the rush hour, and there was a long **tailback**.
There's always **congestion** in the city centre.
You have to pay a **toll** on the new motorway.
Overnight snow caused **disruption** this morning on many roads.
examples.note: disruption = when things are prevented from continuing as usual

lesson.heading: Accidents
lesson.text: A **pile-up** is a crash between several or many cars; a **head-on collision** is two vehicles hitting each other directly in the front. If you **skid**, you lose control of the steering and the car slides across the road. Traffic may be **diverted** - directed away from its usual road.

examples.text: There was a **pile-up** involving ten cars because of the fog, so we were **diverted** onto a narrow country lane.
The road was wet and I **skidded** on a bend and almost crashed.
There was a **head-on collision** on the main road last night.

lesson.heading: Parking and tempers
lesson.text: A **tow-away zone** is an area where your car may be taken away if you park illegally, and a car that is **clamped** has a metal device fitted to a wheel to stop it moving. **Road rage** is anger or violence between drivers caused by difficult driving conditions.

examples.text: I had stupidly parked in a **tow-away zone** and came back to find my car had gone!
I only parked for a few minutes, but when I came out my car had been **clamped**.
I saw two men fighting next to their cars. I think it was a case of **road rage**.

lesson.heading: Informal driving expressions
rows: all the traffic in all directions is unable to move
stop at the side of the road
a small accident without serious damage (informal for collision)
an irritating passenger who tells the driver how to drive

lesson.text: A tailback is the queue of traffic; congestion is the condition that causes it; gridlock is when nothing can move at all.

exercises.prompt: We can't park here; it's a ___ zone.
exercises.explanation: A tow-away zone is an area where your car may be removed if you park illegally.

exercises.prompt: There was a five-mile ___ on the motorway because of road works.
exercises.explanation: A tailback is a line of slow or stopped traffic.

exercises.prompt: Fog caused a number of ___, one of which involved 15 cars.
exercises.explanation: A pile-up is a crash between several or many cars.

exercises.prompt: It was a ___ accident, but the police have a description of the car.
exercises.explanation: In a hit-and-run accident the driver runs into someone and does not stop.

exercises.prompt: The permitted level of ___ is to be lowered in an attempt to reduce air pollution in big cities.
exercises.explanation: Exhaust emissions are the waste gases produced by a vehicle.

exercises.prompt: He was given a ___ test and it was discovered he had consumed a huge amount of alcohol.
exercises.explanation: A breathalyser is an instrument you breathe into to measure your alcohol level.

exercises.prompt: He was charged with drink-driving, fined and given three ___ points on his licence.
exercises.explanation: Penalty points are negative points added up over time, which can result in the loss of your licence.

exercises.prompt: People are being encouraged to leave their cars at home in an effort to reduce ___ in the city centre.
exercises.explanation: Congestion is a situation in which there is so much traffic that it cannot move.

exercises.prompt: 'As I drove round the corner, there was some ice on the road and I lost control of the steering.' - 'Oh, so you ___.'
exercises.explanation: To skid is to lose control of the steering so that the car slides across the road.

exercises.prompt: 'The road was closed. Two lorries had come straight at each other and crashed.' - 'Oh, so it was a ___.'
exercises.explanation: A head-on collision is two vehicles hitting each other directly in the front.

exercises.prompt: 'The police officer fined me there and then. I have to pay within seven days.' - 'I didn't know they could give ___.'
exercises.explanation: An on-the-spot fine is given at the scene of the offence.

exercises.prompt: Match each informal expression with its meaning.

pairs.right: traffic in all directions unable to move
stop at the side of the road
a small accident without serious damage
a passenger who tells the driver how to drive

exercises.statement: A car that is roadworthy is in a condition in which it can be driven safely.
exercises.explanation: Correct - and that includes a minimum depth of tyre tread.

exercises.statement: If your car has been clamped, it has been taken away by the police.
exercises.explanation: A clamped car has a metal device fitted to a wheel to prevent it from moving; a car taken away has been towed away.
